breadcrumb.name: Solar System Size for Daily kWh Usage

sections.h2: How many kW solar system do I need?
p: Divide the units you use a day by the units one kW of solar makes a day in your city. For 15.8 units a day in Lahore that is 15.8 ÷ 4 = 3.95 kW. The yield figure is a yearly average that already includes real-world losses, so the system makes more than your usage in summer and less in winter, and over a year it roughly balances.
Because you buy whole panels, the installed size is 7 × 585 W = 4.1 kW, a little above the calculated figure. Installers sell by inverter size, so this house would be quoted as a five kW system.

sections.h2: Solar system size calculator for Pakistan: why your city changes the answer
p: The same 15.8 units a day needs 4.1 kW in Lahore but only 3.51 kW in Quetta, because a kW of panels makes 5.3 units a day there against 4 in Lahore. Lahore's winter fog and summer dust cost real output; Quetta and Karachi have clearer skies. The table below shows the system size for the same daily usage in every city we have data for.
The city yields come from the Global Solar Atlas long-term averages for panels at the best tilt. A flat-mounted or partly shaded array makes less, so treat the result as the minimum.

sections.h2: Solar calculator by units: a system for five hundred or three hundred units a month
p: If you only have the bill, leave the daily box empty and enter the monthly units. Five hundred units a month is 16.4 units a day and needs 4.11 kW, installed as 8 panels, 4.68 kW, in Lahore. Three hundred units a month is 9.9 units a day and needs 5 panels, 2.93 kW.
Use the bill for the months you want covered. A summer bill with the AC running is usually two to three times the winter bill, and a system sized on the winter bill will not cover summer.

sections.h2: Solar system for a home in Pakistan: what the kW figure does not tell you
p: The kW here matches your energy over a month. It does not check that the panels can carry the house at noon without the grid: an inverter AC, a fridge and fans running together may need more kW at midday than the energy rule gives. If you want to run the AC on solar alone in daylight, size from the appliance list with the solar system from loads calculator and take the larger answer.

You will also need an inverter sized for the running load, not the panel kW, and a battery only if you want backup after sunset. The inverter size calculator and the solar battery size calculator cover those.

sections.h2: How much roof does the solar system need?
p: Each 585 W panel needs about 2.6 m², so 7 panels take about 18.1 m² of unshaded roof, plus walkways. A large house using 40 units a day needs 18 panels on about 46.4 m². Water tanks, stairs and a parapet shadow all cost panels, so measure the clear area before you fix the size.

faq.q: How many kW of solar do I need for 16 units a day?
faq.a: About 3.95 kW in Lahore, installed as 7 panels of 585 W (4.1 kW). Quetta needs 3.51 kW for the same usage because of its stronger sun.

faq.q: What size solar system for five hundred units a month?
faq.a: Five hundred units is 16.4 units a day, which needs 4.11 kW: 8 panels, 4.68 kW installed, in Lahore. Leave the daily box empty and enter the monthly units to see your city.

faq.q: What size solar system for three hundred units a month?
faq.a: About 2.47 kW in Lahore: 5 panels of 585 W, 2.93 kW installed, making about 355 units a month.

faq.q: Is this solar system size calculator made for Pakistan?
faq.a: Yes. The sun yields are Global Solar Atlas long-term averages for Pakistani cities, the defaults are a 230 V home, and the result is in kW and panel count the way installers quote here.

faq.q: Does the system make exactly the units I use?
faq.a: On a yearly average, about 498 units a month for the 4.1 kW system. Summer months make more and winter months less, and net billing carries the difference between months.

faq.q: How many units does a one kW solar system make per day?
faq.a: About 4 units a day in Lahore and 5.3 in Quetta as a yearly average, after real losses. Pick your city above to see its figure in the table.

faq.q: What inverter and battery go with this system?
faq.a: The inverter is sized mainly from the appliances that run at once, and must also accept the panels (most take an array up to about 1.3 times their rating); the battery from the units used after sunset. Use the inverter size calculator next, then the solar battery size calculator if you want backup.

key_facts: Solar system size in kW = units used a day ÷ the units one kW of solar makes a day in the city; 15.8 units a day in Lahore needs 3.95 kW, installed as 7 panels of 585 W.
In Lahore one kW of solar makes about 4 units a day over the year, in Quetta about 5.3, so the same 15.8 units a day needs 4.1 kW in Lahore but 3.51 kW in Quetta (Global Solar Atlas).
A bill of five hundred units a month is 16.4 units a day and needs a 4.68 kW system (8 panels) in Lahore; three hundred units a month needs 2.93 kW (5 panels).
Each 585 W panel needs about 2.6 m² of roof, so a 4.1 kW system takes about 18.1 m² and a 10.53 kW system about 46.4 m².
mistakes: Using the inverter kW as the system size. The inverter is sized from the running load; the panels from the daily units. A five kW inverter with three kW of panels makes three kW of solar.
Reading the meter once. Take two readings a day apart at the same hour, or average a week, before you trust the daily figure.
Sizing on a winter bill. Summer usage with the AC is far higher; size on the months you want covered.
Assuming label watts all day. The yield of 4 units per kW a day in Lahore already includes losses; a quote that promises much more per kW is quoting a clear summer noon.
Forgetting the net-billing cap. The DISCO allows net billing only up to the sanctioned load, so a 10.53 kW system needs a matching connection.

how.text: Daily usage = 15.8 units (from the daily box, or monthly units ÷ 30.42). In your city one kW of solar makes about 4 units a day averaged over the year, with heat, dust, wiring and inverter losses already removed. System size = 15.8 ÷ 4 = 3.95 kW. With 585 W panels that is 7 panels, 4.1 kW installed on about 18.1 m², which should make about 498 units a month.

examples.title: 10 units a day in Lahore
examples.text: 10 ÷ 4 units per kW a day = 2.5 kW. 5 panels of 585 W, 2.93 kW installed, about 12.9 m² of roof, making about 355 units a month.

examples.title: Solar system for five hundred units a month
examples.text: Five hundred units ÷ 30.42 days = 16.4 units a day. ÷ 4 = 4.11 kW, installed as 8 panels of 585 W, 4.68 kW, making about 569 units a month in Lahore.

examples.title: Solar system for three hundred units a month
examples.text: Three hundred units ÷ 30.42 days = 9.9 units a day. ÷ 4 = 2.47 kW: 5 panels, 2.93 kW installed, about 355 units a month in Lahore.

examples.title: 16 units a day in Quetta
examples.text: Quetta makes 5.3 units per kW a day, so 15.8 ÷ 5.3 = 2.98 kW: 6 panels, 3.51 kW installed, making about 566 units a month. Stronger sun means one panel fewer than Lahore.

examples.title: Large house using 40 units a day in Lahore
examples.text: 40 ÷ 4 = 10.01 kW. 18 panels of 585 W, 10.53 kW installed on about 46.4 m², making about 1,280 units a month. Above five kW, check the sanctioned load and net-billing cap with your DISCO first.

content.answer: A home that uses 15.8 units a day in Lahore needs a solar system of about 3.95 kW, installed as 7 panels of 585 W (4.1 kW) on about 18.1 m² of roof, making about 498 units a month. Solar system kW = daily kWh ÷ the units one kW makes a day in your city.

formula.text: kW = E_day ÷ yield; panels = ceil(kW × 1000 ÷ W_panel); kW_installed = panels × W_panel ÷ 1000; units_month = kW_installed × yield × 30.42
lines: E_day = units used a day (or monthly units ÷ the days in an average month)
yield = units one kW of solar makes a day in your city, losses included
W_panel = watts of one panel; panels are rounded up
units_month = what the installed system should make in an average month

content.safety: The panels, DC isolators, earthing and the connection to the house and the grid must be installed by a licensed electrician or a certified solar installer, and a grid-tied inverter must shut off when the grid fails.
